session_covered: US session of Friday 6 November (markets shut over the weekend)
intro: Covers Friday 6 November's US session, the most recent close (markets were shut over the weekend). SPI futures could not be pinned to a single level, so section 2 gives a range.
footnotes: Nasdaq +1.09% is derived from the 24,579.42 close (one source rounded to +1.3% for the Nasdaq 100). Dow close 51,285.73 per two sources; a third cited 51,277. Gold, iron ore, Brent, AUD/USD and the 10-year yield are Trading Economics CFD/reference prices.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (Dec 2026) are up modestly: TradingView shows 9,036 (+0.22%), while Investing.com's Friday-close print is 9,048.5 (+0.03%). The sources agree on direction but not level, so the futures are up roughly 0.03-0.22% (level 9,036-9,048.5; midpoint 9,042, +0.13%). Applied to Friday's ASX 200 close, that implies an open around 9,032, up about 11 points (+0.13%), approximate. The ASX 200 closed Friday at 9,020.80, down 44.27 points (-0.49%), though it gained 1.3% for the week.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data release identified for Monday.
Later this week: Westpac consumer sentiment (Tuesday 10 November, 10:30 AEDT), the business survey and RBA Deputy Governor Hunter speaking (dates not confirmed).
what_moved: A strong US October jobs report (payrolls +165,000 vs about 65,000 expected, unemployment 4.1%) lifted the 10-year yield to 4.87% and pushed up the odds of a Fed rate hike, weighing on the Dow. Chipmakers led a rebound after Thursday's worst session since April 2025, which had put the Nasdaq into correction; technology was the best-performing S&P 500 sector and consumer staples the weakest (sector percentages not available). The dollar firmed and gold slipped.

news.headline: US jobs beat forecasts.
news.summary: October payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 forecast, with unemployment at 4.1% and wage growth above expectations, raising expectations of a Fed hike.

news.headline: Chips rebound after Thursday's rout.
news.summary: Nvidia rose about 3.9% and AMD about 10.8%, but the Nasdaq still fell 3.4% on the week after AI-spending worries.

news.headline: RBA hiked to 4.85%.
news.summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate 25 bp in a 6-3 vote, its fifth hike this year, with guidance seen as less hawkish; markets price about a 6% chance of a December hike.

news.headline: Australian dollar slides.
news.summary: AUD/USD fell 0.95% to 0.6864, its lowest in months, on the global equity sell-off and US midterm-driven worries about tighter AI regulation.

news.headline: Oil steady on Iran risk.
news.summary: Brent held near US$98 as traders weighed possible renewed US action against Iran and the stalled Strait of Hormuz talks; one account says it fell over 12% on the week.

news.headline: Gold dips on the dollar.
news.summary: Gold fell 0.42% to US$4,070.41/oz as the jobs data firmed the dollar, but gained over 4% on the week.

news.headline: ASX 200 slips on Friday.
news.summary: The index fell 0.49% to 9,020.80 as BHP and Rio Tinto dropped with copper at its lowest since July; the major banks rose 0.6-2.7%.

coming_up: US October CPI is due Tuesday 10 November at 13:30 UTC (00:30 Wednesday AEDT; one calendar lists a different day), with headline expected around 0.3% m/m. US PPI follows on Friday 13 November.
